card.name: Word right after a drug or stopping phrase
card.fires_on: A small linking or verb word (if, has, followed, by, with) that comes right after a drug name or a discontinuation phrase in warning text. It marks where the clause's main verb or condition is about to start.

modes.label: If after discontinue
modes.description: The word 'if' right after 'Discontinue [drug name]' before a condition such as serotonin syndrome.
modes.example: Discontinue Promethazine HCl and Codeine Phosphate Oral Solution<< if>> serotonin syndrome is suspected.

modes.label: Has after drug or event noun
modes.description: The verb 'has' following a drug, overdose or effect noun, as in 'has not been established' or 'has been associated'.
modes.example: co-administration of erythromycin with ergotamine or dihydroergotamine<< has>> been associated with acute ergot toxicity

modes.label: Followed by after discontinuation
modes.description: 'followed' or 'by' in a phrase about recovery after stopping therapy.
modes.example: Discontinuation of NSAID therapy was usually<< followed>> by recovery to the pretreatment state.

card.plain: It marks the small joining word right after a drug name or a stop-the-drug phrase, just before the rest of the sentence.
